step_by_step_reasoning:
1. **Identify Nodes**: 
   - Top-left User (`UserConsumerWeb`) making requests via HTTPS to EC2.
   - Legacy .NET Monolith running on `EC2`.
   - Event router using AWS `Lambda`.
   - Fan-out messaging using AWS `SNS`.
   - SQS queues for microservice decoupling: Top Queue (`SQS`), Bottom Queue (`SQS`), and Dead Letter Queue (`SQS` DLQ).
   - Custom application suite (`ThirdParty`) named Crypt Keeper (comprising Morktician, MorkDB, Lazarus) that stores and revives dead letter messages.
   - Operator/Internal user (`UserCompanyDeveloper`) accessing the Crypt Keeper management interface.

2. **Identify Flows & Edges**:
   - **Flow 0 (Event Processing Pipeline)**:
     - User -> EC2 (HTTPS requests)
     - EC2 -> Lambda (Generates events)
     - Lambda -> SNS (Publishes events)
     - SNS -> SQS Top Queue & SQS Bottom Queue (Fan-out event distribution)
   - **Flow 1 (Dead Letter Management & Replay)**:
     - SQS Bottom Queue -> DLQ (Moves unhandled/fatal error messages)
     - DLQ -> Crypt Keeper (Consumes and stores failed messages into MorkDB)
     - Team Member -> Crypt Keeper (Inspects/monitors dead letters via Morktician UI)
     - Crypt Keeper -> SQS Top Queue (Lazarus scheduled process replays/revives dead messages back into queue)

graph.name: MindTouch - Modernizing Legacy .NET Applications
graph.notes: Architecture showing how MindTouch modernizes a legacy .NET monolith on EC2 using Lambda, SNS, SQS, and a custom dead-letter handling application called Crypt Keeper.

nodes.name: User
nodes.notes: External user interacting with the application via HTTPS.

nodes.name: EC2 Monolith
nodes.notes: Legacy .NET application running on EC2 that processes web requests and emits events.

nodes.name: Event Router Lambda
nodes.notes: Serverless function that receives events from the EC2 monolith and routes them to SNS.

nodes.name: SNS Topic
nodes.notes: Fans out events to subscribed SQS queues for downstream microservices.

nodes.name: SQS Top Queue
nodes.notes: Queue supplying messages to target microservice worker.

nodes.name: SQS Bottom Queue
nodes.notes: Queue supplying messages to microservice worker; routes fatal errors to DLQ.

nodes.name: Dead Letter Queue
nodes.notes: Holds unresolvable or fatal messages sent from processing queues.

nodes.name: Crypt Keeper
nodes.notes: Custom system containing Morktician UI, MorkDB, and Lazarus replay engine for dead letter management.

nodes.name: Team Member
nodes.notes: Internal developer/operator managing dead letters through the Crypt Keeper web interface.

edges.notes: User sends HTTPS requests to the EC2 monolith.
Monolith generates events and invokes Lambda.
Lambda publishes event payloads to SNS topics.
SNS delivers messages to SQS top queue.
SNS delivers messages to SQS bottom queue.
Fatal errors or exhausted retries are moved to the DLQ.
Crypt Keeper consumes messages from DLQ into MorkDB.
Team member views and manages dead letters in Crypt Keeper.
Lazarus revives dead messages and replays them back into target SQS queue.
